subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Cardio-oncology: cardiotoxicity patterns, strain echocardiography and surveillance algorithms

steps.tx: Chemotherapy-induced cardiac injury is categorized into two distinct mechanistic paradigms. **Type I cardiotoxicity** exemplified by anthracyclines doxorubicin and daunorubicin is dose-dependent, irreversible, and characterized by myocyte vacuolization and myofibrillar dropout. In contrast, **Type II cardiotoxicity** caused by anti-HER2 monoclonal antibodies like trastuzumab is dose-independent, reversible, and devoid of ultrastructural myocyte death, manifesting as stunning of intact contractile elements.

left.title: Type I (Anthracyclines)
points: Permanent myocyte death and fibrotic replacement
High risk of progressive congestive heart failure

right.title: Type II (Trastuzumab)
points: Absence of myocyte necrosis on biopsy
High rate of LVEF recovery upon drug cessation
Re-challenge often safe after ACE-inhibitor recovery

steps.tx: Anthracycline cardiomyopathy risk escalates exponentially beyond established cumulative exposure ceilings. For **doxorubicin**, the incidence of clinical congestive heart failure rises sharply above a **cumulative dose** of 450 to 550 mg/m2. Prior mediastinal radiotherapy, pre-existing hypertension, or concurrent cyclophosphamide lowers this safety threshold, necessitating early screening and strict lifetime cumulative dose accounting across all treatment lines.

Avoided except in extreme salvage circumstances

steps.tx: Primary cardioprotection during necessary high-dose anthracycline exposure uses targeted catalytic inhibitors. **Dexrazoxane** is an intracellular iron-chelating bisdioxopiperazine that competitively inhibits **topoisomerase II-beta**, preventing anthracycline-induced double-strand DNA breaks and reactive oxygen species generation. Indicated for metastatic breast cancer patients receiving cumulative doxorubicin exceeding 300 mg/m2 who require continuation, dexrazoxane significantly reduces cardiac events without compromising tumour response rates.

nodes.label: Competitive Inhibition of Topo II-Beta & Iron Chelation

steps.tx: Advanced echocardiography detects subclinical myocardial deformation long before ejection fraction deterioration. Two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography evaluates **global longitudinal strain** GLS. A relative reduction in **GLS reduction** greater than 15% from pre-treatment baseline defines early subclinical myocardial dysfunction, directly predicting subsequent left ventricular ejection fraction LVEF drop, triggering prompt initiation of cardioprotective beta-blockers and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors.

A relative reduction in GLS greater than 15% from pre-treatment baseline defines early subclinical myocardial dysfunction, predicting subsequent ejection fraction drop and prompting early neurohormonal therapy.

steps.tx: Unchecked immune checkpoint activation can unleash fulminant autoimmune lymphocytic myocarditis. **Checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis** is a medical emergency with mortality approaching 50%, typically emerging within the first 6 to 12 weeks of anti-PD-1 or anti-CTLA-4 therapy. Characterized by elevated high-sensitivity troponin and conduction blocks, management mandates immediate permanent immunotherapy cessation, telemetry admission, and emergency **methylprednisolone** at 1,000 mg intravenously daily.

rows: First 3 to 12 weeks of ICI therapy
Early surveillance with baseline & serial troponins
Deploy if no troponin decline within 48 to 72 hours

steps.tx: Fluoropyrimidine antimetabolites exert acute coronary vasomotor toxicity independent of underlying atherosclerosis. **Fluoropyrimidines** 5-fluorouracil and oral capecitabine induce direct vascular endothelial injury and severe **coronary vasospasm**, causing resting angina, ischemic ECG changes, or cardiogenic shock during continuous infusional schedules. Management requires immediate infusion termination, sublingual nitrates, and intravenous calcium channel blockers, with secondary re-challenge generally contraindicated.

left.title: 5-FU Vasospasm Presentation
points: Resting angina during or immediately post-infusion
Associated with transient coronary endothelial dysfunction

steps.tx: Vascular endothelial growth factor inhibition regularly triggers systemic endothelial dysfunction. **VEGF inhibitors** bevacizumab, ramucirumab, and multikinase inhibitors like sunitinib and lenvatinib cause de novo **arterial hypertension** in up to 80% of patients. Driven by decreased endothelial nitric oxide synthase activity and capillary rarefaction, effective blood pressure control utilizing ACE inhibitors, dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, or ARBs is mandatory to avoid hypertensive encephalopathy or intracranial haemorrhage.

steps.tx: Electrophysiological repolarization abnormalities require proactive baseline and on-treatment vigilance. Serial **QTc interval** electrocardiographic monitoring is mandatory for targeted small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitors and CDK4/6 inhibitors such as **ribociclib**, sunitinib, and vandetanib. Corrected QT prolongation exceeding 500 ms or increasing by more than 60 ms from baseline demands immediate drug withholding, correction of serum potassium and magnesium, and discontinuation of concurrent QT-prolonging antiemetics.
